properties.description: 4 cases, tools/test_reflow2_check.py::RemoteLocatedArtifact, driven end to end against the built binary and a real throwaway graph. TWO BEHAVIOURAL: a `https://` location is not reported `missing_artifact`, and the gate says "not judged" naming which artifact it could not judge. TWO COUNTERWEIGHTS, and without them the fix would be a way to HIDE drift: a genuinely absent local path is still `missing_artifact`, and an ordinary relative path is not mistaken for a URI (the pattern is anchored and scheme-shaped, not a bare "://" search). MUTATION-CHECKED 2026-08-22: disabling the new branch failed exactly the two behavioural cases and left both counterweights green; restoring it returned all four to green — so the check has been observed red and is known to be capable of failing.
properties.findings: 4 of 4 passing. Observed RED first: the pre-fix gate reported "FAIL DRIFT art:remote: missing_artifact" on a design whose only fault was registering a document at its URL, which is the bug reproduced rather than argued. After the fix the same design reports a note naming the unjudged artifact and exits clean.
properties.name: A URI-located artifact is neither called missing nor silently passed
